newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha firmer reflecting overnight crudes.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha firmer reflecting overnight crudes.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha extended Wednesday's gains in modestly active afternoon trade on Thursday, reacting to an overnight crude rally, traders said.
"There are still buyers on the market despite higher naphtha levels," one trader said. "This means some dealers are expecting naphtha prices to go up further."
Open-spec naphtha for second-half November was bid at $205.00, while offers were heard at $206.00. It was assessed at $203.75/$204.25 in late Wednesday trading.
First-half December was quoted at $204.00/$205.00. It was traded twice at $203.00 on Wednesday.
In spreads, first-half November/first-half December was discussed at plus 75 cents/$1.25, and second-half November/second-half December at plus $1.50/$2.25.
In physical naphtha trading, petrochemical end-users have started working on first-half November cargoes, traders said.
"They are in the market because they don't think prices go down very much further any time soon," one trader said.

There are end-user requirements for five to six cargoes for first-half November arrival, traders said. Levels for November cargoes were notionally assessed at $1.00 to $2.00 over the mean of Japanese quotes. --Tokyo Commodities (81-3 3432 8837)
